newsitem.title: USA: Forbes says new presidential bid possible.
newsitem.headline: Forbes says new presidential bid possible.

text.p: Publisher Steve Forbes said on Thursday it was still too early to say whether he would consider a run for president in the year 2000, but he may decide after next year's congressional elections.

"In 2000 on the Republican side it's wide open," Forbes told Rotarians at a luncheon as he ran through a list of possible rivals for the Republican nomination who included defeated vice presidential candidate Jack Kemp, retired Gen. Colin Powell, Ohio Representative John Kasich and Texas Gov. George W. Bush.
"I'll see what happens in '98. There may be a frontrunner then or a crisis that creates somebody like the Gulf War did for George Bush. Circumstances change," Forbes said.
The multi-millionaire publisher ran for the Republican nomination in 1996 and won primaries in Delaware and Arizona. He spent over $25 million of his own money on the campaign.
